comment: Delivered work packages. A capability may only be advertised in misa / compiler -march / reference capability once every implementation task named for it in config/capability_ladder.json appears here. An ID is added only after that package's own registered cases have been run from a clean build and observed to pass; the evidence column records what was run and where the log lives. In particular the DUT-side evidence for I-005 and I-006 includes mutants that were rebuilt and confirmed to FAIL, because a test that cannot detect a defect it claims to cover has verified nothing.

I-001.notes: All 28 negative controls rejected illegal configurations; the controls refuse to run when the unmodified configuration is already broken.

I-002.notes: 16 negative controls rejected; tag/ABA arithmetic proven against the real geometry. build/p0/rtl/mosaic_id_pkg.svh is generated from these contracts.

I-003.notes: Unknown profiles exit 2 with no fallback; a configuration that does not check out produces no manifest.

I-004.notes: All four registered cases pass. The DUT is an explicitly labelled test double so the harness is proven before any real core exists; nothing it observes is evidence about the core.

I-005.notes: 97069 checks over 3189 cycles. Mutants MOSAIC_FIFO_MUTANT_DROP_ON_FULL, _PHANTOM_POP, _UNSTABLE_OUT and _STALE_RESET were each rebuilt here and each makes the case FAIL with exit 1.

I-006.notes: Mutants MOSAIC_RAM_MUTANT_COMB_READ, _NO_BYTE_ENABLE, _EARLY_VALID and _ARRAY_RESET were each rebuilt here and each makes the case FAIL with exit 1. Collision contract is READ-FIRST byte by byte.

I-015.notes: Case PASS from a clean build (build/p0/unit/<case> removed first) with the official runner: 5263 per-cycle shadow comparisons over 5311 cycles. Six mutants in rtl/core/mosaic_prf.sv each exit 1 with a failure-count delta against the base, per the report; the integration lead verified the case, not the mutants. Same-cycle write-through, bank-conflict serialization, never-written and generation-mismatch reporting are all checkable from rtl/core/mosaic_prf.sv.

I-019.notes: Case PASS from a clean build with the official runner, seeds 1/2/3/12345. The CSR table (addresses, resets, write masks, write-legality) is generated from config/csr/mode_m.json into build/p0/rtl/mosaic_csr_pkg.svh and build/p0/sim/mosaic_csr_table.h, so the RTL and the independent C++ model read one table. Seven mutants each exit 1 with a 0->1 failure delta. NOT verified here: the retire unit's half of the trap contract, mip application, interrupts and privilege violations (all named in the report).

I-020.notes: Case PASS from a clean build with the official runner: 17238 per-cycle shadow comparisons over 5784 cycles, 1471 offered traps (MEI/MSI/MTI), seeds 1/2/7/12345/999983. Seven mutants each exit 1 with a distinct named first failure and a comparison-count delta, and the elaborated model hash differs from the clean build for every mutant, which is the non-vacuity property this project requires. NOT verified: the integrator's half of the boundary contract, the CSR wiring, mideleg beyond bits 3/7/11, analog metastability.

I-016.notes: Case PASS through the official runner with the pre-existing cases `retire.head_block_and_dual`/`commit.head_block_and_dual` unchanged in scope. Seven mutants (the six original plus MOSAIC_ROB_MUTANT_GEN_LOW_BITS_ONLY) each rebuild, differ from the shipping binary and exit 1. Integration follow-up recorded in the report: the ROB's identity widths were 12 bits (2*ROB_INDEX_W) while config/contracts/interfaces.json freezes rob_gen = clog2(rob_entries)+1 = 7; both TAG_W and GEN_W now come from build/p0/rtl/mosaic_id_pkg.svh, and the testbench wrapper derives the same widths from the same package. The wrapper previously re-derived the RTL's own expression, which is why the disagreement had never been observable.

I-014.notes: Both cases PASS through the official runner; the single-width case is the pre-existing one and is evidence that a group of one behaves exactly as before. Six mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary, exit 1 with a 0->1 failing-check delta; the six I-013 mutants were re-demonstrated at their documented first mismatches, so the two-wide refactor preserved the earlier evidence. A real defect was found and fixed in the file: the second commit lane's supersede test compared lane 1's tag with itself (a continuous assign reading a variable assigned in the same always_comb block sees the settled value), so a dual retire released no mapping and leaked one physical tag per two-wide retirement; it survived because the retire case never checked the rename free set. NOT verified: profile p0 only; a checkpoint presented in the same cycle as an allocation is still a known corner (assigned to the lane as a follow-up, since the integrated core takes a checkpoint per branch dispatch); journal_overflow under a two-wide group is argued rather than run. Round 3 of the mutant re-verification independently confirmed all 6 two-wide mutant rows (exit 1, exactly the claimed first mismatches and per-row check totals 9/13/5/9/11/11 at abort) and additionally caught two mutants in the live RTL that no package report claims: MOSAIC_RENAME_MUTANT_CKPT_ALLOC_LEAK (twowide/random:1890, a checkpoint allocation leak) and MOSAIC_RENAME_MUTANT_NO_BOUNDARY_CHECK (squash_accepted expected 0 got 1 at cycle 5831 in the twowide-ckptbad phase). Both are now covered by this case and by I-013's. Recorded drift, not a defect: the package report's section 5 base numbers (9750/9818/16 checks, 'seven two-wide phases') are stale -- two checkpoint phases were added after it was written and the live figures are 9767/9843/18 -- and its sha256 prefixes no longer reproduce because the case sources changed. The mutant claims are what the record rests on and they are confirmed; the stale base figures are noted here rather than silently re-pinned.

I-025.notes: Case PASS through the official runner. Six mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary and exit 1 with a delta: drop-on-collision, valid-as-a-pulse, exception dropped by a following ordinary result, occupancy off by one, kill delivering the killed entry, kill not counted. Valid is holdable rather than a pulse, a same-cycle collision loses nothing, and an exception payload is never overwritten. NOT verified: no consumer yet (I-026), so the result-to-PRF write, the value-visible wakeup and the bank arbitration are untested; only the p0 geometry was elaborated; no timing or area claim.

I-022.notes: Case PASS with 93878203 checks over 199800 cycles (up from 56848546 before the audit: the uop_meta_t fields are now compared per grant and per slot, so the check count rose rather than the coverage shrinking). Audit findings: the randomised phase consumes the whole remaining cycle budget by design and compares every cycle; a directed refused-insert phase was added and the previously undiagnosed 'does a refused insert advance the allocation pointer' question is now covered by a permanent mutant MOSAIC_IQ_MUTANT_REFUSED_INSERT_ADVANCES; zero phase assertions read a live port after the clock edge (one violation was found and fixed). Eight mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary, exit 1 with a distinct named first failure and a delta. --max-cycles is now a hard abort that names the phase. Interface change: ins_meta/grant_meta/obs_meta (mosaic_uop_pkg::uop_meta_t) replace the 4-bit alu_op field; the meta swap mutant fails by name.

I-017.notes: Both cases PASS (the second is the card-named alias for the same binary), 469499 per-cycle shadow comparisons at seed 1. Seven mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary, exit 1 with a +1 first-failure delta. The verdict on the original failure: the DUT was right and the testbench was wrong -- the module decides head_trap on the head alone (not gated on completeness, and taking priority over a recovery flush), events follow the ack rather than the request, and a flush cycle retires nothing. Two mutants that previously produced a zero delta are now detected because the case gained a per-cycle retire_req comparison: a mutant that cannot fail is not evidence, and this package turned two of them into real ones. NOT verified: no external reference model (the oracle is the in-file shadow plus the real ROB and rename); no RTL lint from this package (no RTL changed); the soak is 4000 random steps, not exhaustive.

I-012.notes: Case PASS (1155304 checks, 76192 shadow comparisons, 1238 directed operations, 98 cancellations, 2 killed results, measured latencies 65/33) and decode.rv64im_reserved must also be re-run because this package extended the decoder. Seven mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary, exit 1 with a failure delta (flush ignored, drop-unready, result stuck, div-by-zero constant, W ignored with +113726, unstable result, and the new decoder W_FORMS_ILLEGAL). One mutant was DELETED as vacuous: MOSAIC_DECODER_MUTANT_RV32_WORD_LEGAL mutated the decoder into the behaviour the shipping build now has correctly. ISA defect found by this package and fixed: the decoder trapped RV64I addw/subw/sllw/srlw/sraw as reserved (they are mandatory); OP-32 is now decoded in full (5 I-word forms + 5 M-word forms, reserved patterns re-derived, legal set 10 of 1024), and I-010's report carries an appended correction with binutils evidence. NOT verified: no integration (no ROB/IQ consumer, no result credit, no late-writeback path), p0 geometry only, and the three unreachable W high-half combinations have no external oracle.

I-010.notes: Case PASS from a clean rebuild (169534 checks over 166733 instructions: 82384 legal, 84349 illegal, 1443 named reserved checks). Verified independently by the integration lead: the shipping binary passes and MOSAIC_DECODER_MUTANT_W_FORMS_ILLEGAL makes it fail with exit 1 and 2 named failures. Correction recorded: the package originally asserted that the RV64I word-arithmetic forms (addw/subw/sllw/srlw/sraw) are reserved on RV64 -- they are mandatory RV64I, opcode 0111011 with funct7 0000000/0100000. The decoder, the package comment and the testbench model are fixed, the case now tests the five forms positively, and the vacuous mutant that encoded the old assumption is deleted. The second half of the package (I-011, the integer ALU) has its own case alu.boundaries, PASS.

I-028.notes: Case PASS from a clean build (build/p0/unit/<case> removed first). Six mutants each rebuilt, shown to differ from the shipping binary, exit 1 with a +1 first-failure delta: stale response accepted; identity matched on the id alone without the generation; latency collapsed to one cycle; credit not returned on a kill; request/response sharing one channel (the circular-wait blocker); identity dropped from the response. The header states the recycling rule the card demands: a killed request's entry may be handed to the next request, so a late response is matched against the pairing table and dropped as stale and counted (o_stale_rsp_ctr) rather than delivered. NOT verified: no real remote functional unit or router behind the far side (the far end is a testbench model with a selected fixed delay); no formal no-deadlock proof (structural argument plus a bounded drain test); reset while the far end is still driving is not exercised; counters are proved non-wrapping only within the runner's cycle budget; no route/steering field (that is I-029).

I-024.notes: Case PASS from a clean build (build/p0/unit/<case> removed first): 4366 per-cycle shadow comparisons over 4462 cycles, soak coverage 1231 grants / 635 releases / 592 cancels / 1246 stale ids / 1559 contended cycles / 639 same-cycle terminal+grant / 26 all-pools-full cycles. Six mutants each exit 1 with a distinct named first failure and a check-count delta. A seventh mutant (the credit term dropped) passes identically and is reported as a redundancy probe rather than as evidence: occupancy is derived from the lease ledger and every live lease holds one credit, so at this geometry 'no record free' implies 'no credit free'. The falsifiable form of that defect (a dropped FU class) was written instead and is caught. The card's blockers are the ones tested: all-or-none grant, a refusal with no side effect, and a cancel returning the credit exactly once. NOT verified: p0 geometry only (the driver asserts the geometry so another profile fails loudly); the generation ABA bound is documented, not closed; no real requester exists yet (I-025/I-026/I-028 provide the plumbing); reconfiguration (FREEZE/DRAIN/REVOKED/INSTALL) belongs to I-031; fairness is observed, not proven.

I-033.notes: Case PASS from a clean build: 83805 checks over 4118 cycles, 336 loads, 181 stores, 332 memory transactions, 185 misaligned traps, 50 access faults, 517 responses. The RTL (written by the integration lead, verified by an independent lane) was found correct and was not edited; two defects found were in the testbench and were fixed, both by deciding from the specification rather than from the DUT: the memory model wrote the payload's low byte instead of the byte in the lane the address selects (the module's documented lane convention says the byte at addr is lane addr[2:0]), and a hand-written sign-extension constant for a signed halfword was wrong while both the DUT and the model's own SpecExtract agreed. All four mutants exit 1 with a named first failure and a check-count delta against the base 83805: NO_MISALIGN_CHECK caught at cycle 295 (a misaligned access is forwarded to memory instead of trapping), NO_SIGN_EXTEND at cycle 17, NO_STORE_SHIFT at cycle 35, FAULT_AS_ZERO at cycle 259. NOT verified: no physical memory (a byte-array model: no SRAM, cache, MMIO, coherence or ECC); single outstanding transaction only (I-043 is out of scope); don't-care fields (wstrb/wdata on a load, rsp.data on a store or fault) hide any defect confined to them; only size codes 0..3 driven; one hart; seeds are 400 random transactions, not an exhaustive proof.

I-018.notes: Both cases PASS from clean builds (build/p0/unit/<case> removed first), 419470 per-cycle comparisons over 6810 cycles in the base run. Nine mutants each exit 1 with a distinct named first failure and a delta; two of the previously delivered mutants did not elaborate at all and had never been run (they were re-expressed so they build and still inject the described defect) and three more were added so that each RTL defect fixed has a mutant failing on the check written for it. Root causes the package found: an allocation at the undo bound was accepted while the journal index wrapped (out-of-bounds write, found with AddressSanitizer -- this was the cause of the changing first divergence the integration lane kept seeing, not a shifting model); a restore undid only the restored checkpoint's own branch tag, leaking one tag per killed younger checkpoint; alloc_seen/last_alloc_gen were not reset so the first ROB_ENTRIES allocations after reset reported a regression on a compliant producer; and the credit kill was by epoch-only, which kills older work the squash does not own -- plan section 1.3 and the card forbid it, so the module's documented rule was wrong and its header was corrected rather than only its code. NOT verified: the module still owns its own copy of the speculative maps, free list, generation table and journal; the rename/recovery cutover (one owner for that state, recovery driving rename's ckpt/squash) is recorded in PROGRESS as the next integration task and is not claimed here.

I-008.notes: Case PASS; 39 corpus ELFs, 2774346 architectural events, every retire stream byte-identical to the independent reference (the event comparison is per instruction, not an end-state check; the run is registered at --max-cycles 4000000). Five mutants re-run independently: four exit 1 with the documented first mismatches, and MOSAIC_BRINGUP_MUTANT_4 exits 0 -- its own report section 8.4 declares it unobservable by construction in this profile (every writable CSR is idempotent under a write of its own value), so acceptance criterion 3 is recorded as NOT MET for that one control rather than counted as evidence. That is a coverage gap in the package, not a hardware defect, and it is carried in the report and in results/PROGRESS.md.

I-011.notes: Case PASS: 108560 ALU and 49536 branch vectors, 316022 checks, zero failures; boundary coverage includes 0, all-ones, signed MIN/MAX, W sign-extension, JALR bit-0 clearing and target alignment. Nine mutants re-run independently: all nine exit 1 with the first mismatches their report claims. The case also asserts the invariant that a caller driving branch_taken with no branch named gets is_taken = 0 (the port list defect that produced this package's original wrong fix is now a check, not a comment).

I-021.notes: Case PASS. Five mutants re-run independently: all five exit 1. The discriminating coverage the card names is present and asserted: BTB aliasing is distinguished (two PCs colliding on one index resolve to different targets, and a retrained pair must HIT, so a predictor that always missed cannot pass), training is observable in both directions (a static predictor fails), and reset determinism is byte-identical across two runs. Sizes come from the generated config package (512/64/16), and the module takes no mispredict input by design -- it is corrected by being rewritten from resolved values, with the redirect and miss invariants checked every cycle.

I-007.notes: The independent host oracle and the firmware corpus. 39 cases computed; the oracle agrees with the declared expectations and with the recorded golden signatures, and every program's three inputs produce three distinct signatures -- that last check is what stops a program whose output does not depend on its input from passing. The corpus is crt0 + linker script + trap handler + tohost/UART record + signature region, with fixed expected signatures produced on the host, not by the DUT: the failure mode the card names (comparing the DUT against values the DUT itself produced) is structurally impossible here. Exercised end-to-end by I-008's bring-up case, which compares the DUT's architectural event stream against this oracle's reference per instruction, not on an end state.

I-009.notes: Case PASS from a clean build. Seven mutants, each documented in the report with its injected defect, the phase that catches it, the check count at abort and the first failing field; the report also requires `cmp` to show the mutant binary differs from the shipping one, so a mutant built from a stale object cannot masquerade as evidence. Independently re-verified here: the base passes, and MOSAIC_FETCH_MUTANT_ACCEPT_STALE (the response accepted on the strength of the slot alone) exits 1 after 223 comparisons at cycle 17 with the report's exact first failure, out_valid(registered): expected 0, got 1. The case's discriminating coverage is the redirect path: a late response that belongs to a cancelled slot must be dropped and its credit returned exactly once, which is what four of the seven mutants target; the other three cover the outstanding-request bound, the compressed-form check and the fault path.

V-008.notes: The architectural event interface is frozen (config/contracts/event_v1.json: schema version 1, 21 fields, 100 octets per record, kinds RETIRE/TRAP/MEM_VISIBLE) and the checker is wired into `make check` in both modes; both exit 0. 33 built-in negative controls, each one a single mutation of the interface itself, are all rejected -- the rejections name the offending field and producer rather than an aggregate count, and they cover the three-producer agreement directly: an RTL tap declaration renamed, a host record field removed, a host field widened, a codec field narrowed or reordered or dropped, a codec schema version bumped alone, and a kind table whose values disagree. The freeze is enforced at runtime too: the encoder refuses an encode whose declared version differs from the compiled schema version and the decoder rejects a differing header. Reported gaps, all explicit: no runtime encode->decode->text round trip of a live stream yet (V-010/V-013); three fields are declared pending_rtl with reasons on every run (insn_bits, pc_after, trap_epc, rule F-3); MEM_VISIBLE has no DUT-side producer yet (F-4) and the host RetireEvent must migrate to the canonical record (F-5); p0 has no cache/MSHR/MMIO event tap and no asynchronous-interrupt kind; one hart. Integration route frozen as route A (SV retire probe -> C++ canonical event -> reference adapter); route B (Difftest generator via DPI) is permitted only after the V-004/V-008 layout/timing tests and must keep the same canonical event and serialiser.

I-026.notes: Case PASS from a clean build: 956 per-cycle comparisons over 522 cycles, 11 phases, 194 completions, 23 same-bank collisions, a full 0..127 generation sweep including the 127->0 wrap, all four banks covered, and a phase in which a consumer reads the woken (tag, generation) out of the elaborated register file on the cycle after its wakeup -- the value-visibility claim observed rather than argued. Both models the case uses are documented rules, not the modules: rename's write rule and the ROB's identity-liveness rule are C++ models (the case compiles neither mosaic_rename.sv nor mosaic_rob.sv), and the durable value is read back through the PRF's own read ports. Eight mutants, each ifdef-asserted present exactly once, each rebuilt from a wiped build directory with a binary hash differing from the shipping one, each exiting 1 with a distinct named first failure and cycle: EARLY_WAKE (stale-result cycle 21, a PRF write for a stale result), SAMEBANK_DROP (cycle 75, offered != published), STALE_WRITES, DUP_WRITES, ROB_STALE_WRITES, WAKE_NO_WRITE, RT_TAG_ONLY, WR_CTR_PUB. No mutant passes identically. Independently re-verified here: the base passes with the reported numbers, and SAMEBANK_DROP exits 1 at cycle 75 with the reported first failure. One limitation recorded rather than smoothed over: the ready table keys on the numeric generation and has no reallocation input, so a generation number recycled onto the same tag while its entry is still live answers 'written' until the new producer writes. That is correct under the table's literal contract and is a cross-module width property (7-bit rename generation against the number of allocations a tag can live through), not something this module's ports can fix; it is in the RTL header and the report. NOT verified: p0 and seed 1 only; rob_cmp_bad_uop never driven; store-heavy mixes not stressed; dispatch's actual use of the ready table and the retire consumer of the stash are other packages.

I-013.notes: Case PASS from a clean build (5646 per-cycle comparisons over 5686 cycles, checks=9, base RESULT line byte-identical before, after and between mutant campaigns). Mutant evidence independently re-derived in round 3 of results/reports/mutant-reverification-2026-10-01.md against both rename cases: of 13 mutant defines in rtl/core/mosaic_rename.sv, 7 exit 1 in this case with exactly one failure at the claimed cycle and signal (NO_GEN_CHECK ownership:212, X0_ALLOC x0:1399, NO_FREE_RESTORE squash:1527, NO_EXHAUST_CHECK exhaustion:1678, NO_DUP_WB_GUARD ownership:14, NO_DOUBLE_FREE_CHECK ownership:171, plus CKPT_ALLOC_LEAK random:1890), and the 6 that pass are expected-inert here because five of them target the two-wide path (alloc2_req is never asserted in this single-width case) and one needs the two-wide checkpoint phase -- they are caught by rename.same_cycle_chain instead. Spot-checked here: NO_GEN_CHECK rebuilt and observed to exit 1 at cycle 212 with free_stale: expected 1, got 0. The ownership rule this case exists for is that a physical tag's free/owner state is only correct at its current generation, and that a recycled generation cannot make a stale release look live.

V-011.notes: ELF loader and memory-boundary verification. Case PASS from a clean build: 490 checks, 312 DUT cycles, 13 malformed images rejected and 1 accepted. The rejection contract is exit code 2 with dut_cycles=0 -- a bad image must be refused before the machine is allowed to run, which is the card's fail mode ('a wrong image keeps running') made impossible rather than merely checked. Three real loader defects were found by the new checks and fixed, none by weakening a check: e_type was never read so a dynamic ET_DYN image was accepted at its link-time address; a PT_LOAD whose vaddr+memsz or offset+filesz wrapped uint64 made a wild entry look mapped (both sums are now checked before addition and the segment containment test is overflow-safe); and p_flags was never read, so an entry inside a segment declaring itself non-executable was accepted. Six compile-time mutants each rebuild from an empty directory, differ from the shipping binary, and exit 1 naming the check they break; tools/check_elf_load.py independently re-parses the image and agrees byte for byte, and exits 1 on a corrupted manifest. Regression-checked here: harness.bad_image (I-004) and core.bringup_vs_reference (I-008) still pass and the golden signature check still agrees. Recorded judgement call: the p_flags==0 carve-out that keeps the I-004 image loadable. NOT verified: p_align is read but only the 8-byte rule is enforced; ET_NONE/ET_REL refused but not exercised against real images; the DUT checks prove image delivery and the first retire, not retire semantics or a run to TOHOST. All numbers were produced after the V-009 lane restored sim/tb/mosaic_bringup_tb.sv (wrapper sha256 78c27dfe..., HEAD 29bb23d).

V-009.notes: Reset and initial-state replayability. Case PASS from a clean build: 440 checks over reset lengths of 1, 2, 5 and 17 valid clock edges crossed with four release instants (high after the last edge, on the falling edge, low before the first edge, in a late low phase), plus abort/restart at S_FWAIT, at S_DWAIT, at the accepted TOHOST store and at a seed-chosen edge count, plus a same-seed replay of every configuration with bit-identical post-release state. The card's fail modes are the ones tested: no architectural event is reported while reset is asserted, no device write occurs during reset, and an old transaction cannot cross reset into the new run. Five negative controls all fail as required -- two in the core (an event reported in reset; mscratch surviving reset) and three in the environment model (the clear pass leaving RAM alone; an outstanding fetch/data transaction surviving reset; the end-of-run latch surviving reset). The package found and fixed a real defect in sim/tb/mosaic_bringup_tb.sv: the reset branch cleared the TOHOST-written flag but not its one-cycle commit latch, so a reset landing in that window made the restarted run report end-of-run on its first live edge with an empty event stream -- precisely the pollution the card forbids -- and the fix is guarded by a mutant that now fails, proving the line is load-bearing. It also found and fixed a vacuous abort in its own case (the TOHOST abort fired one cycle before the memory model accepted the store, so it never actually reset an outstanding transaction). Independently re-verified here: the case passes and core.bringup_vs_reference still passes. NOT verified: reset polarity as a waveform (only synchronous active-high exists in this RTL, so edge-sampled deassertion is proven but neither an asynchronous nor an active-low path); zero reset edges (undefined, the smallest tested length is 1); mcycle is excluded from the state comparison because it counts clocks, minstret is compared; privilege is carried by mstatus only because p0 is M-mode; 'queue ownership' is checked in its bring-up analogue (the memory model's outstanding-transaction state) because the bring-up core has no queue -- the package itself says this must be re-pointed at the integrated core's ROB/rename allocation state when that lands, and that re-pointing is not claimed here.

I-023.notes: The integrated core runs end to end for the first time: fetch, decode, rename, dispatch, two clusters, WB/PRF, ROB, retire and recovery are one machine and the registered case passes from a clean build -- checks=59, comparisons=678, cycles=129, retires=17, c0_alu=8, c1_alu=8, muldiv=1, max_occupied=6. The card's two fail modes are covered by controls rather than argued: MOSAIC_DISPATCH_MUTANT_SINGLE_CLUSTER (the second cluster never used) exits 1 at cycle 129 with o_c1_alu_ctr=0, and the out-of-order claim is visible in the numbers rather than asserted -- uop index 13 completed at cycle 49 while index 12 completed at 114, with retirement still in program order. Two real integration defects were found by this driver and fixed in mosaic_core.sv, both left with a negative control: the 2-entry decode buffer wrote slot 0 whenever nothing was popped, overwriting a live entry left in slot 1 by a pop, so the machine retired two instructions out of program order (observed allocation order 0,2,1); and rename's committed map was fed the ROB entry generation instead of the physical tag's generation -- same width, different counter -- so 'speculative map == committed map' was false from the first commit onward, which is the boundary every redirect and the I-018 checkpoint path rests on. After both fixes retirement order is exact and o_rename_boundary is 1 at every quiescent point. Independently re-verified here: base PASS with the reported numbers, SINGLE_CLUSTER exiting 1 at cycle 129. NOT covered, and this is a first-integration case rather than a core-complete one: no branches in the program, so the branch barrier, the redirect arbiter inside the core, cluster purge and fetch redirect are unexercised; no load/store/CSR/trap/interrupt/fence/MMIO/cache/multi-hart (dispatch refuses them and the data port is never asserted); one MUL/DIV encoding; one seed; p0 only. Two gaps stated rather than claimed: a same-cycle grant offered by both clusters never occurs (dispatch allocates one macro per cycle and alternates affinity, so the streams are staggered by construction) and the decode buffer's vacated-slot invalidation is not reached by any stimulus the lane could build -- its mutant passed and was removed rather than left in the tree as a false control.
